title: Adherence Nudge Channel Volume
scenario: A digital pharmacy runs an adherence intervention experiment targeting patients overdue for chronic medication refills. The care team sends SMS, email, and in-app push notifications to prompt refills.
prompt: The stakeholder proposes tracking 'Total nudge messages sent per week' as the key metric to evaluate which channel drives the most refill behavior. What is wrong with this metric?
instructions: One short sentence: name the flaw, propose a fix. No formulas required.
stakeholder_rationale: More messages sent means we're reaching more patients, so we can compare channels by volume.

numerator.label: Refills completed within 7 days of nudge
Patients who opened the nudge message

denominator.label: Nudge messages sent in the channel
Eligible patients in the intervention cohort
Active app users in the period

guardrail.label: Average days overdue at time of nudge

metric_movers.reason: Care team expands eligible patient cohort to include 14-day-overdue patients
metric_movers.explanation: Larger eligible cohort receives more messages, inflating total volume without changing per-channel effectiveness.

metric_movers.reason: SMS delivery vendor rate-limits messages during peak hours
metric_movers.explanation: Technical constraint reduces SMS send volume without reflecting actual channel performance.

metric_movers.reason: Email subject line A/B test improves open rate from 22% to 31%
metric_movers.explanation: Better subject lines increase engagement but total messages sent remains unchanged.

metric_movers.reason: Push notification volume drops as more patients disable app notifications
metric_movers.explanation: Reachable push cohort shrinks, lowering total push messages sent regardless of refill impact.

metric_movers.reason: Care team shifts from 3 reminder cadence to 5 reminders per patient
metric_movers.explanation: Increasing messages per patient inflates total volume without changing which channel drives refills most effectively.

metric_movers.reason: Pharmacy switches PBM contract, changing formulary coverage
metric_movers.explanation: Formulary changes affect refill feasibility independently of nudge channel effectiveness.

metric_movers.reason: Marketing team launches a brand awareness campaign on social media
metric_movers.explanation: Brand campaign does not change nudge message volume or refill rates for the intervention cohort.

metric_movers.reason: Patient portal redesign changes color scheme and typography
metric_movers.explanation: Cosmetic UI changes do not affect adherence nudge messaging volume or refill behavior.

expected_themes: not normalized per patient or per message
reference_answer: Total messages sent measures volume, not effectiveness. Use Refill Conversion Rate (refills completed within 7 days / nudge messages sent) to compare channels.

grading_rubric.criterion: Identifies that the metric is a raw count, not normalized
grading_rubric.description: Answer explicitly states the flaw is lack of normalization or that volume does not measure effectiveness.

grading_rubric.criterion: Proposes a rate metric with refills in numerator
grading_rubric.description: Corrected metric is a ratio with refills completed (or similar outcome) divided by messages sent or patients nudged.

grading_rubric.criterion: Names the correct denominator (messages sent or patients)
grading_rubric.description: Denominator is nudge messages sent or eligible patients, not total app users or unrelated population.
Answer matches PAA terseness: flaw + fix in under 30 words.

hints: Think about what the stakeholder is actually trying to learn about each channel.
A channel that sends 10x more messages but converts fewer patients is not better.
What denominator would let you compare effectiveness across unequal send volumes?
common_mistakes: Proposing a per-patient metric but forgetting to normalize by messages sent (each channel may send different message volumes per patient).
Suggesting open rate as the fix when the goal is refill behavior, not engagement.
Focusing on message deliverability issues instead of the normalization flaw.

_meta.scenario: a patient adherence intervention tracking which nudge channels move refill behavior
